description: The night sky: a still star field behind the Start page, after Netscape Navigator's throbber, over a dark planet whose limb stands low below the Omnibar, its glow pulsing, with comets and shooting stars falling from the upper right and going out behind the limb, a larger comet now and then falling in front of the planet, and streaks falling thick and fast from a commit until the page paints (#590, #629). The browser draws it (src/ui/NightSky.qml); the website does not. Lengths are shares of the scene's width or height unless named otherwise; times are in seconds. A colour is a role (ground, light, glow, skyTop, skyLow, face, black, white) or a mix of two at an amount. A gradient stop is [position, colour] or [position, colour, alpha]. A [from, span] range is scattered from `from` to `from + span`. `crt` is the CRT glass the sky declares, which the host draws, with the road's amounts. `rest` is where the Omnibar rests, as a share of the height. `omnibar` is how wide it stands where the browser hands in no width, as a thumbnail has it: `widest` CSS pixels at most, `inset` narrower than the scene, and its field's top `above` CSS pixels over where it rests. `planet` is the dark planet rising from the bottom, after Navigator's globe: its top, the glow along its limb included, stands `share` of the way from the resting Omnibar's bottom edge, whatever it holds, to the scene's bottom. The browser hands that edge in as `omnibarReach` below where the Omnibar rests, at the theme's type size here. Where `share` would leave the limb's ends less than `edgeClear` CSS pixels above the bottom, where the Shortcut sheet's cue stands, the planet stands higher, but never less than `gap` CSS pixels below the Omnibar. Its `radius` is a share of the width, its face the ground darkened by `face`, its limb a line `width` CSS pixels wide (at `unlit` alpha of the light in a Private window, where it has no glow), and the glow along it `reach` CSS pixels out, its opacity pulsing down to `pulse.low` of its peak and back every `pulse.every` seconds. `comets` fall in slots of `every` seconds: a slot whose scatter is over `chance` holds a group, one to three by the cumulative shares in `together`, each starting `apart` after the one before, up to `most` in the sky at once. Each falls `slope` down the diagonal from the upper right toward the lower left, placed by where it goes out behind the limb, `out` along the width, and appears `run` of the width up the diagonal from there, fading in over `fadeIn` seconds. A comet that started before the sky was last shown afresh, on its first frame, after its clock jumped, or after it changed size or Omnibar, is not drawn. `steer.share` of them pass the Omnibar's lower right corner instead, their glow `steer.clear` CSS pixels off the field and a scene pixel more, appearing `steer.beyond` of the width before the corner, where their fall still ends within the slot. It falls `speed` of the width a second until its tail of `length` has gone out too. A kind's `share` is the cumulative share of comets of that kind, its tail `width` CSS pixels wide at the head, its `head` and `halo` CSS pixels across. `head` and `halo` at the top are their colours. `still` is the one comet reduced motion holds, `at` of the way down its run. `front` is the comet that falls in front of the planet, in slot `at` of every `every`, with no other comet in that slot: `after` seconds into it, it comes in from the right edge on a line `angles` [from, span] degrees below the horizontal, scattered for each crossing, that passes the resting Omnibar's lower right corner with its glow `steer.clear` CSS pixels off the field and a scene pixel more, where its light catches the rim. Where that line would leave the bottom edge less than `exit` of the width from the left, it comes in lower. and leaves through the bottom edge `lasts` seconds later, its trail fading over `fades` seconds. A slot the streaks fell in keeps no front comet. Its `length`, `width`, `head` and `halo` are as a comet kind's. As it crosses, `flare` lights the planet up to `peak`, the face drawn as `flare.face` and the glow along the limb with `flare.glow`. `glint` is the light a passing comet casts on the Omnibar's rim, as the road's `light` is the sun's: an ellipse centred on the head of the comet in front of the planet while it crosses, else of the comet above the limb whose ellipse reaches furthest over the Omnibar's field, `across` of the Omnibar's width and `reach` CSS pixels down, and the bloom over it. `streaks` fall down the comets' diagonal from a commit until the page paints.
name: Night sky
